_comment: Luna's Work asset source catalog: which source fits which asset kind (kinds = KINDS of src/lunasworkAssetPipeline.js). Read by src/lunasworkAssetCatalog.js; the Director (casting) and the Critic (judging) use it as a fixed menu. costClass: free = a free library, local = runs on this PC, paid = spends Higgsfield credits. needsKey = an API key in LunaCore's asset key store is needed to import from the source (Higgsfield uses its own CLI login, so it is false there). ComfyUI model families come only from the AMD GPU rule (AMD_GPU_RULE). Higgsfield model ids and credits verified 2026-11-25 on the work PC with higgsfield CLI 1.2.2, workspace Private selected: every id below is listed by `higgsfield model list --json` and answers `higgsfield model get <id> --json` (gpt_image_2_6 = GPT Image 2.6, nano_banana_flash = Nano Banana 2, seedream_v5_pro = Seedream 5.0 Pro, flux_kontext = Flux Kontext, text2image_soul_v2 = Higgsfield Soul 2.0, multi_image_to_3d = Multi-Image to 3D). Credits for the five image models are the CLI's own `higgsfield generate cost <id> --prompt ...` answers at default params (0.75, 1.5, 2.5, 1.5, 0.12). The 3D model's 30 credits is an ESTIMATE kept from the old table: `generate cost multi_image_to_3d` cannot price without real image references (its validation rules are unsupported by the cost endpoint). Credits are per-final planning figures (CLI-priced except the 3D estimate) and are the one source of truth for the spend estimate (src/lunasworkAssetCost.js reads them from here).

sources.toonFit: Mostly photoreal scans and PBR textures: usable for shapes and layout, but every asset needs a toon pass (flat colors, cel shader, outlines). HDRIs only light a scene.
Mixed styles from many authors: search for stylized or low-poly downloadable models; photoreal ones need a toon pass.
Low-poly with flat colors: a good fit for a toon / cel-shaded game, usually only a material swap to the toon shader.
PBR textures and HDRIs: realistic surfaces; use them as a base for hand-painted or flattened toon textures, not as they are.
Large SFX and ambience library; style-neutral, a good fit for SFX after normalization.
Photoreal museum scans with dense meshes: needs retopology and a toon pass; best as reference or for rare props.
Mixed styles, many realistic: pick stylized models; the rest need a toon material pass in Blender.
Sound effects library; style-neutral, a good fit for SFX.
Local drafts: prompt for cel-shaded, flat-color, clean-outline styles; image results are drafts, 3D results need cleanup and a toon material.
Modeled to the art direction through the Blender MCP: the best fit, toon shading and outlines are built in from the start.
Paid finals: strong at stylized and anime-like images when the prompt asks for cel shading; 3D results still need a toon material.
